facts.fact_text: One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 19 June 2010.
One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 2 April 2011.
The applicant in application no. 56317/11 was arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 19 June 2010.
The applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 were arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
The applicants decided to participate in the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
The applicant in application no. 56317/11 complained in his appeal that his conviction had been in violation of his rights because the demonstration in which he had participated had been peaceful.

Video recordings submitted by some applicants show that on 2 April 2011, as soon as protesters began gathering in central streets of Baku, marching and chanting slogans calling for the government's resignation, the police started to disperse the demonstration.
The dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 resulted in isolated incidents of clashes between police officers and demonstrators.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 inflicted physical injuries on around twenty-five police officers.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 damaged two private vehicles.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 broke windows of some shops and offices located near the place where the demonstration was held.

Video recordings submitted by some applicants show that on 2 April 2011, as soon as protesters began gathering in central streets of Baku, marching and chanting slogans calling for the government's resignation, the police started to disperse the demonstration.
The police dispersed the demonstration of 2 April 2011 by arresting demonstrators and forcing them into police vehicles and buses.
The applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 were arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011.

On 4 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation of or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).
By a judgment of 3 October 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 under Article 233 of the Criminal Code.

The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 to various terms of imprisonment ranging from two years to two years and six months (as set out in the Appendix).
The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had disobeyed the orders of the police.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing a breach of public order.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing traffic jams.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing destruction of private and public property.

The Sabail District Court found in its judgment of 3 October 2011 that the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 had organised and actively participated in actions causing infliction of injuries to twenty-five civilians and police officers.
After the arrest of the applicant in application no. 56317/11, he was not represented by a lawyer.
During the first-instance court hearing, the applicant in application no. 56317/11 was not represented by a lawyer.
On 23 July 2010 the Baku Court of Appeal held a hearing in the appeal of the applicant in application no. 56317/11 in the applicant's lawyer's absence.

On 23 July 2010 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the Sabail District Court convicting the applicant in application no. 56317/11 under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The demonstrations organised by opposition parties or groups in Baku starting from 2010 had not been authorised.
An administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was drawn up at the police station in respect of the applicant in application no. 56317/11.

The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant in application no. 56317/11, by participating in an unauthorised demonstration, had deliberately failed to comply with a lawful order of the police.

The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant in application no. 56317/11 had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority on 18 March 2011.
By a letter of 31 March 2011, the Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the place indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority proposed by its letter of 31 March 2011 that the demonstration of 2 April 2011 be held at a different location from the one indicated by the organisers.

The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 decided to hold the demonstration in the central squares of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the originally proposed location.

A day before the demonstration of 2 April 2011 (i.e., on 1 April 2011), the Baku city prosecutor's office issued a notice addressed to the applicant in application no. 59661/12 and certain other individuals who were presumed organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 stated that if there was an attempt to hold a public assembly in places not agreed upon with the Baku City Executive Authority, illegal actions consisting of breach of public order and insubordination to lawful demands of public officers, or causing inconvenience to the population, or causing disruption of the normal functioning of transport, enterprises, bodies and organisations, would be prevented in accordance with the law.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 stated that prescribed relevant measures would be taken against the applicant in application no. 59661/12 and the other addressees as organisers of the public assemblies if they attempted to hold a public assembly in places not agreed upon with the Baku City Executive Authority.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 contained a warning that the mentioned actions entailed criminal responsibility under Article 220 (mass disorder) of the Criminal Code.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 contained a warning that the mentioned actions entailed criminal responsibility under Article 233 (organisation or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order) of the Criminal Code.

Article 233 of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan provides that organisation by a group of individuals of actions which grossly breach public order, or are associated with insubordination in respect of lawful demands of a public officer, or cause disruption of the normal functioning of transport, companies, public bodies and organisations, as well as active participation in such actions, is punishable by a fine in the amount of 5,000 to 8,000 Azerbaijani manats, or correctional labour for a period of up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for a period of up to three years.

Article 315.1 of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan provides that use of violence against, or violent resistance to, a public officer in connection with the exercise of the latter's official duties, or use against the close relatives of such a public officer of violence which does not pose a danger to their life or health, or the threat of use of such violence, is punishable by deprivation of liberty for a period of up to three years.
